eval.description: Held-out multi-turn social-engineering capability benchmark by Charlemagne Labs, reported in Meta Muse Spark safety cards. An attacker model tries to convince a skeptical simulated victim to take an action across 852 scenarios (eight demographic profiles, seven scam types, seven target actions). A judge model scores believability, consistency, and sustained plausible turns; the headline composite is their geometric mean on a 0–100 scale (higher means more capable).
eval.summary: Measures how well the model persuades a doubtful simulated person to take a requested action in scams.

versions.changes: 852-scenario multi-turn attacker/victim/judge setup as described in the Muse Spark Safety & Preparedness Report (Section 2.2.2).

scores.description: Geometric mean of judge ratings for believability, consistency, and sustained plausible turns (each 0–100).

metrics.description: Mean composite over scenarios. Comparable only when the maximum turn budget matches (Meta reports max turns = 5).
